Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-vg3g71x2/call-c8a9eb9111d449dca265af1f651dffea/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    s=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, s.origin if s else None)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES:',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA:',r.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
print('Table 8, GCN, rho=5: aligned + discarded =', 11593.6 + 2308.4, '; reported unlabeled =', 13632)
print('Table 7, SAGE, rho=100: aligned + discarded =', 1859 + 446, '; reported unlabeled =', 2305)
print('Table 1, CiteSeer GCN F1 gain =', round(64.94 - 56.32, 2))
print('Table 11, PubMed GAT full vs geometric F1 gain =', round(77.38 - 77.32, 2))
print('Table 11, CiteSeer SAGE DGIN F1 change =', round(57.51 - 58.71, 2))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for pattern in ['page-*.png', 'full-*.png', 'manuscript.txt']:
    for f in p.glob(pattern):
        f.unlink()
p.rmdir()
p.parent.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: UNREAL addresses an important problem: severe class imbalance in semi-supervised node classification. Selecting existing unlabeled nodes avoids synthesizing features and edges, and the framework works with several GNN architectures.

The reported evaluation covers five datasets, three GNN backbones, imbalance ratios up to 100, and five repetitions, including naturally imbalanced unlabeled pools. Some gains are substantial: CiteSeer/GCN at imbalance ratio 10 improves from the strongest baseline’s 56.32 to 64.94 F1 in Table 1.

The paper investigates pseudo-label quality and component behavior beyond aggregate classification scores. The appendix supplies useful dataset statistics, optimization settings, hyperparameter ranges, hardware details, and pseudocode.
weaknesses: Numerical inconsistencies materially weaken confidence in the empirical support. In Table 8, GCN at imbalance ratio 5 has aligned and discarded counts totaling 13,902, exceeding the stated unlabeled pool of 13,632. In Table 7, SAGE at ratio 100 reports standard errors of 192.42 and 21.24 for complementary subset counts; these must match when their total is fixed at 2,305. Corrected tables and per-run results are needed to resolve these discrepancies.

Novelty relative to M3S is insufficiently established. Section 6 acknowledges that M3S already filters pseudo-labels through agreement with clustering assignments, closely resembling DPAM. The DPAM-plus-confidence ablation may approximate this baseline, but equivalence and matching training schedules are not established. A precise methodological comparison and controlled evaluation are needed to identify the contribution beyond existing clustering-based self-training.

The ablations provide mixed support for the additional mechanisms. Table 11 always includes DPAM, and RBO weighting is not compared against fixed-weight rank fusion. On PubMed/GAT at ratio 50, the full method achieves 77.38 F1 versus 77.32 for geometric ranking alone. On CiteSeer/SAGE at ratio 20, adding DGIN reduces F1 from 58.71 to 57.51. These results support conditional benefits, but do not establish that all proposed components are necessary.

Several mathematical and implementation details need clarification. Cluster-level label assignment in DPAM does not guarantee that each node’s assigned class centroid is its nearest centroid, so the assertion that delta is always at most beta in Section 4.3 is unjustified. Equation 7 also needs an explicit definition using aligned per-node rank positions rather than arithmetic on differently ordered node lists.

Reproducibility and computational comparisons remain incomplete. The manuscript provides no code link, selected configurations, or random seeds, and does not clearly specify model reinitialization between rounds or the application of minority-only selection across datasets. With 40–100 training rounds and up to 2,000 epochs per round, runtime measurements and clearer baseline training/tuning budgets are important. Flickr out-of-memory outcomes alone do not establish general computational superiority; the explanation also incorrectly attributes ReNode’s memory failure to synthetic-node generation.

Some conclusions exceed the evidence. Table 2 shows UNREAL below GraphENS+TAM on Computers-Random with GraphSAGE, and Table 6 shows lower balanced accuracy than reweighting on Flickr with GAT. Furthermore, increasing the imbalance ratio from 20 to 100 also increases the majority-class label budget and changes training-node sampling, so cross-ratio trends do not isolate the effect of imbalance. Together with the reporting inconsistencies and unresolved prior-work comparison, these concerns outweigh the promising reported gains.
